title: Fix the Quadratic String Building
description: Stop a report builder from copying the whole report every time a line is added.
statement:
`ReportBuilder` collects the lines of a plain-text report while a job produces them, then returns the finished text.

- `ReportBuilder(title)` starts a report whose first line is the title.
- `add_line(line)` appends a line (given without its newline). `build()` returns the whole report: the title line, then every added line in order, each followed by a newline.
- `build()` may be called at any point, and the report can keep growing afterwards.
- Reports can be huge (hundreds of thousands of lines), so the cost of adding a line must not grow with the length of the report so far.

**Example**

```python
report = ReportBuilder("Daily signups")
report.add_line("web: 120")
report.add_line("mobile: 95")
report.build()    # "Daily signups\nweb: 120\nmobile: 95\n"
```

**Observed:** a 3-line report is instant, but a job that adds 200,000 lines takes minutes, and doubling the number of lines makes it four times slower.

The tests count the characters your code copies while building the text, and look at how the builder stores the report, so a slow version fails at once instead of timing out.

hints: Strings cannot be changed in place. What does `self.text += ...` have to do to produce the new string, and how much does that cost when the text is already 10 MB long?
Do not keep the growing text in a string. Which structure lets you add a piece in constant time and put all the pieces together once, at the end?

Writing the same concatenation another way (an f-string, `format`, `"".join([self.text, ...])`) copies just as much. Also, `build()` can be called at any point and the report can grow afterwards, so it must not throw the collected pieces away.
explanation:
**The bug class: quadratic string building.** Strings are immutable. `self.text += line + "\n"` cannot grow the old string in place: it allocates a new string and copies the old text plus the new line into it. Adding n lines therefore copies about n²/2 lines' worth of characters: harmless for 10 lines, minutes for 200,000, and the time quadruples when the size doubles.

**A common confusion.** CPython sometimes rewrites `s += t` on a plain local variable into an in-place resize, so a simple loop `report += line` can look fast. That is an implementation detail: it does not apply when the string lives in an attribute (`self.text`, as here) or any other place that holds another reference to it, nor to `s = s + a + b`, and other Pythons do not do it at all. Do not build code on it.

**The fix.** Keep the pieces in a list and join them once: `"".join(parts)` adds up the lengths, allocates the result once, and copies every piece exactly once, so the whole job is linear in the size of the report. `io.StringIO` is the other standard tool for this. The same idea applies to bytes (`bytearray`, `b"".join`) and to lists (`result = result + [x]` copies the whole list on every pass, `append` does not).

**Habit.** Whenever you grow a string or list inside a loop, ask whether each step copies everything built so far. If it does, accumulate in a list and finish with a single `join`.
